messages:
oncall-bot: [INCIDENT] High 5xx rate observed for /v1/generate (hosted inference, us-west-2). Alert triggered: error-rate > 5% for 3m. Paging oncall.
emily.c: I'm on it. seeing spike in 5xx from inference-gw behind the LB. digging logs now.
raj.k: FYI I'm with infra-contacts. I will reach out to cloud provider if we see networking or instance issues. tagging @sara_ops for customer comms.
sara_ops: starting status page draft now. do we have estimated impact? which customers hit the route?
emily.c: quick findings: errors are internal 500s from model-proxy (stacktrace includes `KVCache::miss`), not 502 from the load balancer. errors correlate with requests hitting instances with kernel version 5.10. Also seeing increased GC spikes in the logs.
mike_sre: can we snapshot a failing request? `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'` returned 500 with stack mention of `kv_cache:invalid-shard`.
emily.c: snapshot attached (pasted):
```
ERROR model-proxy: KVCache shard 12 mismatch at seq 0
backtrace: ...
env: kernel=5.10, libc=2.31
```
raj.k: looks like a kernel/tls interaction on instances created in last deploy window. rolling window of hosts provisioned in us-west-2 ~ 02:00-03:00 UTC.
ops_lead: decision: escalate to cloud provider network team and also open ticket with upstream model runtime vendor. Raj please open provider escalation and share ticket ID here. Sara draft external status and a customer DM template targeting impacted customers (Dedicated/Private customers with pinned models) and hosted customers who have high usage.
raj.k: opening cloud provider support case now. contact: cloudops-support@cloud.example (tier1) and will request P1 escalation. I'll paste the case number when created.
emily.c: mitigation idea: divert traffic away from suspected hosts via `instance=~"kernel-5.10"` LB rule, and scale up unaffected pool. prepared a quick `lbctl` command: `lbctl update-route /v1/generate --exclude-labels kernel=5.10` — can someone approve quick run?
mike_sre: +1 approve. run it and monitor token latencies and error-rate.
emily.c: executing: `lbctl update-route /v1/generate --exclude-labels kernel=5.10` ... returning 202. initiating rollout.

oncall-bot: Action taken: route update scheduled (id: r-1718000000-1). Monitoring.

(3m later)

emily.c: immediate effect: 5xx rate down from 6.8% -> 1.1%. latency stable. current error-rate 1.0% over 5m.
ops_lead: good. continue to monitor. Raj, any updates from cloud provider?
raj.k: cloud support case created: CS-20240608-9934. I pushed for netops sync — they've assigned an engineer and want logs + core dumps. asked for 2hr ETA on initial findings.
ops_lead: Sara, can you post status page with current mitigation and customer guidance? Keep it factual: we mitigated by routing changes, investigating root cause with cloud + runtime vendor, no evidence of data loss.
sara_ops: draft status page entry (please review):
"We are investigating increased error rates for API path /v1/generate affecting hosted inference in the us-west-2 region. We have applied a routing mitigation to divert traffic from a subset of impacted hosts which has reduced errors. We are actively engaging the cloud provider and the model runtime vendor for a root cause analysis. Impact: customers in us-west-2 may have experienced failed requests and increased retries between 02:00-03:00 UTC; rate-limited customers may have seen elevated error rates. No customer data loss has been detected. Next update: in 60 minutes or when we have new findings."

sara_ops: draft customer DM for high-impact customers (only minimal personalization):
"Hi <CustomerName> — we're reaching out about increased 5xx errors you may have experienced on API requests to our hosted inference in us-west-2 earlier today. We applied a routing mitigation that reduced the errors. We're coordinating with the cloud provider and the upstream runtime vendor to identify root cause and will share updates. If you saw production impact we can enable a temporary regional failover for your account. Apologies for the disruption — reach us at support@redwood.ai or reply here for immediate assistance."

emily.c: small internal comms template for on-call handoff: 
"Handoff summary: Mitigation executed (route exclude kernel=5.10), error-rate reduced to ~1%. Cloud provider case CS-20240608-9934 opened. Kernel version implicated on suspect hosts. Actions outstanding: cloud provider to analyze core dumps; vendor to review KVCache shard handling; confirm if a kernel patch is needed or repro steps exist. Monitoring: error-rate channel + alert threshold to 2%."

ops_lead: I'll take on second-shift handoff. @mike_sre you get primary until 11:00 UTC. please keep escalation fresh and update case with any new core dumps.
mike_sre: got it. I'm collecting core dumps and will upload to case CS-20240608-9934 and to internal S3 at s3://incidents/cs-20240608-9934/cores. I'll redact PII before upload.

raj.k: vendor outreach: emailing runtime-vendor-support@modelvendor.com with subject: "P1: KVCache shard mismatch on kernel 5.10 — CS-20240608-9934". sharing logs and core dump link.

(10m later)

mike_sre: cloud engineer replied: "Prelim: we see a kernel bug in 5.10.72 that can affect io URBs under specific netfilter conditions. Recommend repro on a test host and patch to 5.10.100. We'll coordinate a kernel patch roll for affected instances."

ops_lead: thanks. Plan: keep routing exclusion until hosts are patched or repro proves false. Do not mass reboot hosts during high traffic window. Next steps for the shift: 1) Work with infra to schedule kernel patching on affected host group, 2) vendor to confirm if runtime patch needed, 3) prepare a concise customer follow-up once we have patch timeline.
emily.c: note for postmortem: include timeline of deploys that introduced kernel-5.10 hosts and our LB label hygiene. Also run a rum test to ensure our instance labeling is accurate for automated routing.
sara_ops: posted status page now (ID: status-1718000000). sent customer DM to top 10 affected customers (with SRE on CC). will send follow-up after vendor/cloud patch ETA confirmed.

ops_lead: logging this thread into incident tracker (#INC-2024-06-08-03). please add any artifacts (logs, core dumps, ticket links) to the tracker.
emily.c: adding lbctl diff, logs, and the snapshot to the tracker now.

mike_sre: handing off to @ops_lead for the night shift. if error-rate creeps back above 2% alert me via pager and I'll re-open the routing. Good handoff notes in the incident tracker.

ops_lead: Acknowledged takeover. We'll keep the route exclude in place and coordinate patch schedule with infra. Closing slack thread for live updates; will re-open if new material changes. :lock:"
